evidence_quotes.quote: This paper discusses the issue of water as a human right based upon the analysis of the World Water Forum which has existed since 1997 and involves the public, private and scientific sectors. The qualitative textual analysis was based upon documentation of these events.

o objetivo deste estudo é compreender como a questão da água, enquanto direito humano, vem sendo tratada em nível continental nos Fóruns Mundiais da Água ocorridos entre os anos de 1997 e 2012, a partir da análise textual qualitativa.
Os documentos consultados nesta pesquisa foram extraídos dos Fóruns Mundiais da Água, sendo que a maioria das informações obtidas foi encontrada nos relatórios finais dos respectivos fóruns.
As informações coletadas referem-se à preocupação com a identificação do tratamento concebido à água na condição de direito humano. Para tanto, buscou-se pela palavra chave em inglês “human right”.

Quanto à ocorrência da palavra-chave “human rights”, constatou-se que 33% das ocorrências foram encontradas no 6º Fórum Mundial da Água, seguido do 5º Fórum e do 4º Fórum, os quais representam respectivamente cerca de 27% e 24% do total de ocorrências.

criterion_notes.c1: Although framed around the human right to drinking water, the paper examines international diplomatic and stakeholder discourse in World Water Forum declarations at a continental level rather than actual household or community water or sanitation service access.
criterion_notes.c2: Plain wording vs. narrow 2026-10-13 reading: Under the plain/broad wording of Criterion 2, the paper would satisfy C2 because it examines international human-rights norms (such as UN General Comment No. 15), constitutional recognition, and global governance declarations across the World Water Forums. Under the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type mechanism reading, however, it fails C2 (no) because it analyzes macro-level international summit declarations and normative human-rights rhetoric rather than any operational rule-type mechanism directly governing service access (eligibility screening, administrative burden, documentation or tenure requirements, tariff or cost-recovery rules, discretion or accommodation, enforcement, or utility ownership/regulatory structure empirically governing access).
criterion_notes.c3: The authors conduct a qualitative textual/documentary analysis (citing Moraes, 1999) of final reports from the 3rd–6th World Water Forums and web pages from the 1st–2nd Forums, searching for the keyword 'human right' and summarizing summit declarations. This represents a documentary overview of international conference declarations and normative human-rights texts without any empirical evidence on actual water or sanitation service delivery or access (E05). Even if keyword counting across four summit reports were treated as documentary discourse data, there is no empirical evidence on service access.
criterion_notes.c4: Reports no outcome measuring household, community, or utility water or sanitation access, connection, availability, reliability, continuity, quantity, affordability, or exclusion; reports only thematic summaries of summit declarations, forum attendance figures, and the percentage distribution of occurrences of the keyword 'human rights' across forum reports.
criterion_notes.c5: The unit of analysis consists of conference reports and web pages from six World Water Forums (1997–2012); there is no identifiable household/community population, legal/administrative rule-type exposure, or service-access outcome.
criterion_notes.c6: Published in Portuguese with an English abstract; Portuguese is directly eligible without translation per Criterion 9.

study_design: Qualitative textual/documentary analysis of World Water Forum reports and website pages (1997–2012)
country: Global / multi-continental (documents from World Water Forums held in Morocco, Netherlands, Japan, Mexico, Turkey, and France)
population_and_sample: Official documentation from six World Water Forums (1997–2012): website pages for the 1st and 2nd Forums and final reports (plus continental reports for the 4th Forum) for the 3rd, 4th, 5th, and 6th Forums
outcome: Thematic framing of water as a human right in World Water Forum declarations and percentage distribution of occurrences of the keyword 'human rights' across forum reports (no water or sanitation service-access outcome reported)
rationale: Excluded as E05 (no empirical evidence on service access). Full-text Portuguese article matches the record metadata (Zorzi, Turatti, & Mazzarino, 2016, doi:10.4136/ambi-agua.1861). The paper conducts a qualitative textual summary and keyword search ('human right' / 'human rights') of final reports and website pages from the 1st through 6th World Water Forums (1997–2012) to trace international and continental diplomatic discourse on the human right to drinking water. It contains no primary or secondary empirical evidence on household or community water or sanitation service access (failing C1 and C3), analyzes macro-level international summit rhetoric rather than a rule-type legal/administrative mechanism governing access under the 2026-10-13 C2 clarification (though it passes the plain broad wording of C2), and reports only summit declaration themes, participant totals, and keyword shares rather than any real-world service-access outcome (failing C4 and C5; hence excluded under both plain and narrow C2 readings).
